subject: small blue fish
title: A Whole Species Lives in One Desert Hole. In 2025 Only 38 Were Left

scenes.text: An entire species lives in one hole in the desert.
The Devils Hole pupfish: an inch long, bright blue, in a flooded cave in Nevada.
They feed and breed on one sunlit shelf, eleven feet by sixteen.
In December 2024, an earthquake 500 miles away sent waves through the pool. Another followed in February.
The waves swept the algae and eggs off the shelf. By spring, a count of 191 had fallen to 38.
So for the first time, biologists added nineteen fish raised in a backup tank. A whole species, topped up by hand.

description:
The Devils Hole pupfish lives in one water-filled cavern in the Nevada desert, part of Death Valley National Park: the smallest habitat of any vertebrate species. The water stays about 93 degrees Fahrenheit, and the fish feed and spawn on a single sunlit shelf 11 feet by 16.
The count fell to 35 in 2013 and recovered to 191 by spring 2024. Then a magnitude 7.0 earthquake off northern California in December 2024, 500 miles away, and another quake in February 2025 sent waves through the pool that swept algae and eggs off the shelf; the spring 2025 count found 38. The National Park Service added 19 captive-raised fish, the first time that had been done.
Should people step in to save a species like this? Comment below.
first_comment: Divers have explored the cavern to more than 400 feet and nobody knows how deep it goes. Would you swim in it?
